title: Keep the enduring agent apart from each session's credential, and show a registered agent with no session credential
blocked_by: Tom's or the card lead's sign-off of this brief on its card, before card_build_v3 runs; no row is dispatched before it, and a build started without it is a defect of the chain. The sign-off is also the review of this brief's file manifest (CN9): R1 modifies docs/design/identity/DIRECTORY-CONTRACT.md and R2 creates crates/lys-identity/tests/agent_without_session.rs. Check: the card records the sign-off.

R1 and R2 wait on DIRECTORY-003 landed, which creates docs/design/identity/DIRECTORY-CONTRACT.md and crates/lys-identity/; this brief creates neither and never takes DIRECTORY-003's wall (CN9). The blocker reads DIRECTORY-003's own execution record, not a roadmap row: RM-001 links five briefs, so its status cannot say whether DIRECTORY-003 alone has landed. Check a stranger can run against lys main, from the repository root after git fetch origin: python3 -c "import json,subprocess; c=subprocess.check_output(['git','rev-parse','origin/main'],text=True).strip(); b=json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['git','show',c+':docs/design/directory/briefs/DIRECTORY-003.json'])); print('landed' if b.get('execution',{}).get('status')=='landed' else 'not landed', c)" prints landed followed by the origin/main commit it read; any other first word means R1 and R2 are not dispatched.

R2 waits on the landed lys-identity exposing, in its public API, the registration of an agent under a signed-in person, the directory list and the read of one agent (DIRECTORY-003 R1), and on docs/design/identity/DIRECTORY-CONTRACT.md listing the members of an agent record. If the landed crate keeps its integration tests other than under crates/lys-identity/tests/, or the landed agent record holds a member that carries a session credential, R2 stops and names it, and the act that answers is a revision of this brief through the card's lead (CN9). Check: cargo doc -p lys-identity --no-deps lists the registration, list and read functions, and rg -n 'agent record' docs/design/identity/DIRECTORY-CONTRACT.md prints the line that lists the record's members.
purpose: Road adjustment 3 keeps the enduring agent and each session's credential apart: starting another session never creates another agent, and an agent can be registered before it ever runs. The road and its adjustments live in docs/design/identity/STATEMENT-2026-09-22.md, and this brief cites that statement at lines 162 to 167 as the source of adjustment 3 (the adjustment itself is line 166); docs/design/directory/DESIGN.md does not gain the road or its adjustments. This brief writes the adjustment into the directory's contract, so the road step 2 work that brings sessions inherits it as a rule rather than rediscovering it, and proves the half the directory can show: an agent registered with no session is listed under its responsible person with no session credential.
task: Two rows, in dependency order. R1 adds the contract section to docs/design/identity/DIRECTORY-CONTRACT.md (1 hour). R2 adds one test file under crates/lys-identity/tests/ proving that an agent registered with no session is listed under its responsible person and read with no session credential, keyed on the member list the contract gives the agent record (1 hour). Estimate: 2 focused implementer hours, a new increment stated beside revision 5's ceiling of 48 focused hours and not inside it; an overrun is reported and any change to the ceiling follows CN7. This brief lands now as documents, and its build is blocked until DIRECTORY-003 lands: DIRECTORY-003 creates docs/design/identity/DIRECTORY-CONTRACT.md and crates/lys-identity/, and this brief creates neither. The second done criterion, an agent registered with no session appearing in the directory with no session credential, is proved by this card's build, which runs once DIRECTORY-003 has landed; a person sees the no-credential agent only after DIRECTORY-002 and DIRECTORY-003 are built. This is a contract brief. It keeps the design's non-goal 'Road step 2 onward' and P6 as they read and does not bring sessions or session start into this cluster: no session, session record, session credential type or presentation step is built. The first done criterion, a second session of the same agent presenting the same enduring identity with a new session credential, is written in R1 as rule 5 of the contract. Its proof is blocked on the road step 2 card that brings sessions, carried by roadmap row RM-029 ('A session is its own record, issued at session start and pointing at its agent', road step 2, session start being Chippy's release 3 at docs/design/identity/STATEMENT-2026-09-22.md:156); the check a stranger can run is python3 -c "import json,subprocess; d=json.loads(subprocess.check_output(['git','show','origin/main:docs/design/roadmap.json'])); print(*[i['status'] for i in d['items'] if i['id'] == 'RM-029'])" prints landed. RM-029 carries no card yet, and this brief records that finding so the lead cards it. That card also builds the presentation step by which a started agent reports back and the directory checks it. What a person sees from this brief is the written contract and the no-credential agent, not a working second session. The brief says registered and not provisioned, so the lifecycle document's word keeps its own meaning: registered is the directory's state, whatever grants or handles the agent holds. ADR-011, which is proposed and stays as written, describes registered as 'registered (exists in the directory, no grants, no credential handle, may not act)' and also says 'Having a grant or a credential is a fact beside the state, not a state.'; the second sentence governs the first, so the parenthesis describes what a newly registered identity holds and is not a condition of being registered. This brief does not amend ADR-011. Acceptance checks the session credential and nothing else; the agent's grant and handle counts show whatever they are. The form of the session credential is not decided in this brief. The three readings, a per-session lys certificate, a SpeaksFor delegation and an ADR-001 handle, are recorded as an open question for the road step 2 card. The contract requires only that the session credential be distinct from the agent's one certificate (ADR-008) and never mint an agent. This brief makes no cryptographic change and adds no new consumer of SpeaksFor. DIRECTORY-003 stands: each agent is registered under its responsible person, and every identity change is a signed event; R2 registers through DIRECTORY-003's registration unchanged. Every code row is red first: R2's first commit adds its test file with a failing expectation named, and its second commit makes it pass. Test names are snake_case and carry the criterion ids (d011_r2_ac1 and d011_r2_ac2). No wall clock, no person's name and no date inside code. Every path is relative to the repository root.

requirements.title: Write road adjustment 3 into the directory contract
requirements.spec: The directory contract docs/design/identity/DIRECTORY-CONTRACT.md SHALL gain one section headed '## Enduring agents and session credentials', added after the sections DIRECTORY-003 wrote and changing none of them. The section SHALL cite docs/design/identity/STATEMENT-2026-09-22.md:162-167 as the source of road adjustment 3 and say that the road and its adjustments live in that statement. It SHALL hold these seven rules as a numbered list, in this order: 1. The agent record is the enduring identity, and it holds no session credential. 2. A session is a separate record that points at exactly one agent by that agent's enduring id. 3. Starting a session never creates an agent. 4. An agent may be registered before it ever runs, and while no session of it exists it holds no session credential. 5. A second session of the same agent presents the same enduring agent id with a new session credential. 6. A session credential is distinct from the agent's one lys certificate (ADR-008), and it never mints an agent. 7. A started agent reports back to the directory (ADR-007), and the directory checks what it presents; the presentation step is built by the card of roadmap row RM-029, not by this contract. The section SHALL record as open for the road step 2 card the form of the session credential, naming the three readings: a per-session lys certificate, a SpeaksFor delegation and an ADR-001 handle. It SHALL say that the proof of rule 5 is blocked on the road step 2 card that brings sessions, roadmap row RM-029, and that what this contract delivers is the written rules and a registered agent with no session credential, not a working second session. The section SHALL NOT choose a form for the session credential, name a field, type, wire format or content type for one, give SpeaksFor a consumer, or define a session id format. This row SHALL NOT create docs/design/identity/DIRECTORY-CONTRACT.md, and SHALL NOT edit docs/design/identity/STATEMENT-2026-09-22.md, docs/design/directory/DESIGN.md, docs/design/directory/design.json, the IDENTITY-001 files or any other section of the contract.

requirements.title: Prove an agent registered with no session appears in the directory with no session credential
requirements.spec: WHILE an agent is registered under its responsible person and no session of it exists, WHEN the directory lists its agents or reads that agent, THE SYSTEM SHALL list the agent once under its responsible person (DIRECTORY-003 R1) and SHALL answer its read with exactly the members docs/design/identity/DIRECTORY-CONTRACT.md lists for an agent record, none of which carries a session credential (R1, rules 1 and 4). THE SYSTEM SHALL NOT answer that read with a session credential, a placeholder for one, or a member naming a session. The proof is one test file, crates/lys-identity/tests/agent_without_session.rs, driving lys-identity's public registration, list and read (DIRECTORY-003 R1) with a disposable test identity (CN2); its expected member list is copied from the contract's agent-record list, with the contract line it came from cited beside it, so the check is keyed on what the contract supplies and not on a value the test substitutes. The test SHALL NOT assert or change the agent's grant or handle counts, which show whatever they are. This row SHALL NOT add a session record, a session credential type or a member to the agent record, SHALL NOT create crates/lys-identity/ or docs/design/identity/DIRECTORY-CONTRACT.md, and SHALL NOT change a file of DIRECTORY-003: if the landed record fails the test, the row stops and names the failing member, and the act that answers is a revision through the card's lead (CN9).
acceptance: d011_r2_ac1: a disposable signed-in person registers one agent and no session of it is started; the directory list then returns exactly 1 entry with that agent's enduring id, and that entry's responsible person is the registering person's id.

d011_r2_ac2: the read of that agent, serialized as the public response, has as its top-level members exactly the agent-record member list copied from docs/design/identity/DIRECTORY-CONTRACT.md (the list holding at least 1 member, with the contract line cited in the test), and the count of members whose name contains 'session' is 0.
cargo test -p lys-identity --test agent_without_session prints 'test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed', and rg -c 'fn d011_r2_ac[12]\b' crates/lys-identity/tests/agent_without_session.rs prints 2.
